analysis.title: ONEOK Inc. (OKE): First Take: 3Q26 Effectively In Line and 2026 Raised; Watch for 2027 Comments on Call
key_insights: OKE reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $2,238m vs GSe $2,191m and FactSet consensus $2,165m (+2.1%/+3.4%), but operating results were effectively in line. Transaction and minority equity sale adjustments (~$53m net) appear to drive the headline beat.

Refined Products and Crude segment EBITDA of $685m beat GSe $646m on higher optimization benefits (notably butane blending) and lower costs, offsetting a Natural Gas Liquids shortfall (lower Permian rates drove lower margins despite elevated marketing results).

Management raised the 2026 EBITDA guide to $8.5-8.6b from $8.2-8.5b, vs GSe $8.6b and consensus $8.5b. The ~$200m midpoint increase reflects YTD outperformance and the Brazos acquisition close in 4Q26, which adds ~$75m ($50m net of transaction costs).
Brazos contributions look light vs GS expectations. GS will look for color on the call.
FY26 capex increased to $3.5b from $2.7-3.2b on spending associated with the Brazos Permian Midland acquisition. No meaningful organic projects were announced.
GS expects some modest stock weakness the next day after recent strong performance. Directional commentary on 2027E EBITDA (GSe and consensus $9.2b) is expected to drive sentiment.

GS price target ($91) and estimates are unchanged. Key call questions: base business performance, Brazos integration and implied 2027E EBITDA growth, capital allocation after the Apollo financing, and durability of the long-term EBITDA CAGR target.
Neutral rating with a 12-month price target of $91 based on a 10.25x multiple on 2027 EBITDA. The stock closed at $96.01 on 27 Oct 2026, 5.2% above the target.

market_movers.rationale: Price target and estimates unchanged after a 3Q26 print that was in line at the operating level. The $91 target is based on 10.25x 2027 EBITDA and sits 5.2% below the $96.01 close.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA actual (reported 10/27) $2,238m vs GSe $2,191m and FactSet consensus $2,165m, up 5.5% QoQ from $2,121m in 2Q26. GS says operating results were effectively in line and the headline beat reflects ~$53m of net transaction/minority equity sale adjustments.
3Q26 segment EBITDA actual vs GSe: NGL $718m vs $743m, Gathering & Processing $563m vs $567m, Natural Gas Pipelines $231m vs $236m, Refined Products and Crude $685m vs $646m.
3Q26 dividend actual $1.07, in line with GSe and consensus.

3Q26 volumes actual vs GSe: NGL raw throughput 1,661 kb/d vs 1,665; gas processing 5,866 mmcf/d vs 5,831; refined products shipped 1,615 kb/d vs 1,677 (-3.7%); crude shipped 1,693 kb/d vs 1,774 (-4.6%).
Natural Gas Pipelines EBITDA fell 22.2% QoQ from $297m, driven by narrower Waha spreads vs 2Q26.
2026 EBITDA guidance raised to $8.5-8.6b from $8.2-8.5b. GSe 2026 EBITDA $8,613m, 2027E $9,208.5m (consensus 2027E $9.2b).
risk_factors: Upside risks: higher-than-expected synergy realization, higher commodity prices, higher project returns, stronger cash generation and capital returns, Northern Border quality spec tightening.
Downside risks: expensive M&A, slower asset integration and synergy realization, higher competition for Permian NGLs, softer commodity prices, project execution.
